rationale: Evidence from published cohorts confirms that peripheral nerve involvement in NKX6-2-related spastic ataxia 8 (SPAX8) is an atypical phenotypic expansion rather than an obligatory feature of the disease. In initial descriptions, peripheral nerve electrophysiology was normal or unremarkable, with pathology centered on central nervous system hypomyelination. Bereshneh et al. (2020) documented motor-predominant peripheral axonal neuropathy manifesting as wrist and foot drop in two siblings with the homozygous c.501C>G (p.Phe167Leu) variant. No study in the available literature demonstrates a primary demyelinating peripheral sensorimotor polyneuropathy in SPAX8, supporting the hypothesis that peripheral involvement, when present, is a low-frequency motor-predominant axonal neuropathy.

evidence.text: Bereshneh et al. reported two siblings with a homozygous NKX6-2 missense variant c.501C>G (p.Phe167Leu) who demonstrated wrist and foot drop caused by peripheral axonal neuropathy, describing this as an expanded clinical manifestation of SPAX8.

new_directions.question_text: Does NKX6-2 express in Schwann cells or is axonal loss secondary to lower motor neuron/anterior horn cell degeneration?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether the axonal peripheral neuropathy observed in p.Phe167Leu patients reflects peripheral Schwann cell dysfunction or primary motor neuron axonopathy will elucidate whether SPAX8 pathology extends directly to the peripheral nervous system.

new_directions.question_text: What is the systematic prevalence of electrophysiologically proven axonal neuropathy across all reported SPAX8 kindreds carrying homeobox versus non-homeobox variants?
new_directions.rationale: Systematic EMG/NCS across multiple international cohorts is required to determine whether peripheral axonal neuropathy correlates with specific missense residues or represents an under-reported manifestation of prolonged disease duration.
